newsitem.title: FRANCE: Major swindle at Credit Lyonnais - board member.
newsitem.headline: Major swindle at Credit Lyonnais - board member.

text.p: A member of the state holding company reorganising the troubled Credit Lyonnais state bank accused its officials on Thursday of swindling the bank of five billion francs ($870 million).
Charles de Courson told the National Assembly's financial commission that 52 legal suits had been filed.
"As things now stand, we can expect there will be 100 cases levelled against directors or officials of the bank whose now uncovered swindles total five billion francs," he said in an open hearing.
De Courson said the complexity of the swindles and delays in legal procedures were such that he had little hope most of the funds would be recovered.
De Courson estimated the bank's losses after a spending and lending binge in the late 1980s at 130 billion francs ($22.6 billion).
Credit Lyonnais was at the time briefly Europe's biggest bank before it started declaring the largest losses in French corporate history as property investment and loans went seriously wrong.
The French government said on February 21 it was delaying for more than a month a new rescue plan for Credit Lyonnais.

The surprise decision to postpone the plan, due to be presented that week, came after the European Commission, which must approve state aid packages, sought changes to an outline presented by Finance Minister Jean Arthuis.

A Finance Ministry spokeswoman then said France and the European Commission wanted to limit the amount of public funds poured into the bank, which has already consumed billions of francs in taxpayers' money, and were seeking a fuller rescue plan.
